example_business: Example (K9a, without your own holidays): 2026-06-29 to 2026-07-06, United States: 5 and 6 Monday-to-Friday days, minus the holiday on them (2026-07-03), give 4 and 5 business days.
example_own: Example (K10): with 2026-10-31, a Saturday, as your only own holiday, 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-02 still gives 1 and 2 business days.
example_reversed: Example (K4, without your own holidays): 2026-10-30 to 2026-10-26 is counted as 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30.
example_total: Example (K1, without your own holidays): 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30 is 4 days with the start date not counted, 5 with both counted.
example_weekend: Example (K3, without your own holidays): 2026-10-30 (Friday) to 2026-11-02 (Monday) is 3 and 4 days in total, but 1 and 2 business days: the weekend does not count.
help_business: Business days are the Monday-to-Friday days of the range, minus the holidays of the active calendar and your own. Mexico: the mandatory rest days of the federal labour law; one that falls on a weekend is not moved. United States: the federal holidays; one on a Saturday is observed on the Friday before, one on a Sunday on the Monday after. Switching the calendar counts the range again.
help_elections: Mexico's law also makes the day of an ordinary election a rest day. Federal and judicial elections fall on a Sunday, so they do not change a business-day count. A state's local election can fall on another day and applies in that state only, so it is not built in: if it applies to you, add it to your own list. With Mexico active, a note under the result reminds you.
help_intro: What each part of the page does, and how its counts are made. Each example is a known answer: a range the app's tests check, by reading this guide's own text and counting it again.
help_language: Choose English or Spanish in the bar at the top of the page. The labels, notices and messages change language; the counts and the laws' official titles do not. The choice is saved, and the page opens in it next time; with nothing saved, it opens in your browser's language when that is English or Spanish. In Spanish, business days are "días hábiles", with a note on the different meaning the federal labour law gives that term. The button beside it switches between light and dark, and that choice is saved too.
help_own:
Add the days your work also closes, such as a local holiday or a company day. Each calendar keeps its own list: a day added under Mexico does not count under the United States. The list is saved, so it is still there after a restart. Remove takes a day off, and the counts return to what they were. The status in the bar at the top says whether the list can be read and written: Storage OK, or Storage unavailable, and then no count is shown.

A day counts once: one of your own on a Saturday, a Sunday or a built-in holiday changes no count.
help_past: Holidays follow today's rules in every year: the laws as last checked, listed under Sources. A rule that changed, such as a holiday added or moved, is applied to the years before the change too. So when a range reaches into an earlier year, a notice says that its business days may differ from what applied then. Total days do not depend on holidays.
help_range:
Enter a start date and an end date as YYYY-MM-DD, choose a calendar, and press Count.

Each count is shown two ways, side by side. Start date not counted: the end date minus the start date, as a spreadsheet subtracts two dates. Both dates counted: one more, for when the first day counts too, as in a leave or a stay. Total days count every day; business days are explained below.
help_reversed: If the end date comes before the start date, the page swaps them, counts the range in order, and a notice says so. The counts are those of the dates in order.
help_sources: Under Sources, each calendar lists the laws its holidays come from, with a link to the official text, the date each was retrieved, and the date the rules were last checked against them. A change to a law after that date is not in the app until its rules are checked again.
how_business: The Monday-to-Friday days in the range, minus the calendar's holidays and your own that fall on them, each day once.
how_total: Start date not counted: the end date minus the start date, in days. Both dates counted: one more.
note_business_days: In Spanish this page says "días hábiles": Monday to Friday, minus the active calendar's holidays and your own. Art. 715 of Mexico's Ley Federal del Trabajo gives the term another meaning, for labour proceedings.
note_local_elections: Local election days are not built in: add a state's election day to your own list.
notice_past_years: The range includes past years: holidays are computed with today's rules, and past years may differ.
notice_swapped: The end date was before the start date: the dates were swapped.
